question: For the patients with the normal glutamic pylvic transaminase level, how many of them are male?
evidence: normal glutamic pylvic transaminase level refers to GOT < 60; male refers to Sex = 'M';
clarification: Count each distinct ID only once.
gold: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.GOT < 60 AND T1.SEX = 'M'
gold0: SELECT COUNT(T1.ID) FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.GOT < 60 AND T1.SEX = 'M'

d.request: How many distinct patient IDs are male (Sex = 'M') and have a normal glutamic pylvic transaminase level (GOT < 60)?
d.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'M' AND l.GOT < 60;

b.request: Count the distinct patients whose Laboratory.GOT is less than 60 on at least one laboratory record and whose Patient.SEX is 'M'.
b.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON l.ID = p.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'M' AND l.GOT < 60
b.raw: Count the distinct patients whose Laboratory.GOT is less than 60 on at least one laboratory record and whose Patient.SEX is 'M'.

c.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.ID) FROM Patient AS p JOIN Laboratory AS l ON p.ID = l.ID WHERE p.SEX = 'M' AND l.GOT < 60;
